papers.title: Multi-scale vision transformer model with UAV-based hyperspectral imagery for early identification of pine wilt disease infected trees
papers.authors: Hao Shi, Ruirui Zhang, Meixiang Chen, Huixiang Liu, Danzhu Zhang
papers.abstract: Pine Wilt Disease (PWD), caused by the pine wood nematode ( Bursaphelenchus xylophilus ), is a devastating forest disease characterized by rapid spread and high mortality. During its pathogenesis, the green attack and early stage are critical for disease control. However, RGB UAV images lack obvious visual features at these stages, which limits the accuracy of existing identification methods. This study aims to develop a Multi-Scale Vision Transformer Model specifically designed for UAV hyperspectral data. The primary objectives are to improve the identification capability for the green attack and early stages of PWD. To accurately capture subtle changes in the spectral and spatial features of pine trees during the green attack stage, an efficient spectral-spatial feature fusion module was designed. Meanwhile, an improved Gaussian self-attention mechanism was introduced to enhance the modeling of spectral differences between central pixels and their neighboring pixels. papers.title: Climate-Based Modeling of Invasive Species Impact on Urban Green Infrastructure Using CLIMEX and Remote Sensing Data
papers.authors: A. Suresh kumar, C. Rajan
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of Smart Infrastructure and Environmental Sustainability
papers.abstract: The pace at which invasive alien species are established and spread is becoming a threat, especially to urban ecosystems, due, in part, to the variability of climates, urban growth, and fragmentation of habitats. These biological invasions are highly dangerous to urban green infrastructure (UGI), which sabotages biodiversity, ecological services, and ecological resilience in the long term. A unravelled modelling approach to employ the CLIMEX model of species distribution as well as the spatial analysis of ecosystems via remote sensing to observe invasion risk zones and map them in the fast urbanising landscapes was created in this work. The climatic suitability of chosen invasive species in the current and future climate conditions under parameters serving as temperature, precipitation, and humidity was simulated with the help of the CLIMEX model, and the land cover dynamics and vegetation indices (as well as the urban heat islands) were measured with the assistance of remote sensing data (Sentinel-2 and ModiS) measurements. papers.title: Managing the global invasive pest Drosophila suzukii : Strategies and challenges
papers.authors: Ting Feng, Haiyang Wang, Zeying Wang, Jianhua Huang, Jiani Chen
papers.abstract: Abstract The spotted wing drosophila ( Drosophila suzukii ) is a globally invasive pest that threatens the production of soft‐skinned and stone fruits. Characterized by a serrated ovipositor that enables females to lay eggs in intact ripening fruit, D. suzukii causes direct larval feeding damage and promotes secondary pathogen infections, leading to significant economic losses. Although chemical insecticides remain the dominant control method in commercial systems, their long‐term sustainability is increasingly compromised by insecticide resistance and environmental concerns. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of current management strategies against D. suzukii , covering advances in monitoring techniques, cultural and physical controls, chemical approaches, and biological control utilizing parasitoid wasps, predators, and entomopathogens. We emphasize that the integration of multiple control measures within a systematic integrated pest management (IPM) framework is essential to achieve effective, economically viable, and ecologically sustainable suppression of this pervasive pest.

papers.title: Proposal for monitoring the Eastern Grey Squirrel (Sciurus carolinensis) in Poland
papers.authors: Barbara Kominek, Joanna Gruszczyńska
papers.abstract: The report presents a nationwide, continuous monitoring program for the invasive eastern grey squirrel (Sciurus carolinensis) in Poland, aimed at early detection and prevention of its spread. Monitoring focuses on high-risk areas such as urban parks, deciduous forests near cities, protected areas and border regions. The program includes repeated surveys across seasons using camera traps, field observations, winter nest searches and citizen reports. Grey squirrels pose a serious threat to native fauna, particularly the red squirrel, through competition and disease transmission. Immediate removal of detected individuals, strict enforcement of legal bans, cross-border cooperation and public awareness are emphasized. Effective monitoring combined with rapid response offers a real opportunity to prevent the establishment of this invasive species in Poland.

papers.title: When nematodes take flight: Multi-scale dispersal of the beech leaf disease nematode in forest ecosystems
papers.authors: Erika Consoli, Lily Berry, Niclas Lyndby, Miriam R. Wayman, Lucas W. DeGroote
papers.abstract: Beech leaf disease, caused by the invasive foliar nematode Litylenchus crenatae, is an emerging threat to Fagus grandifolia across North America. Since its initial detection in 2012, the disease has spread to a total of 16 U.S. states and the Canadian Province of Ontario; however, the mechanisms underlying nematode dispersal remain poorly understood. This study evaluated multiple potential dispersal pathways across two forest sites in central Pennsylvania through integrated field surveys, environmental monitoring, and experimental validation. Weekly sampling was conducted to characterize nematode population dynamics in relation to temperature, precipitation, wind, and humidity. Long distance water-mediated dispersal was assessed through creek sampling, while biotic dispersal was investigated through field sampling from migratory bird feet during high-moisture events and a controlled greenhouse transmission experiment. Wind dispersal was further examined in a pilot study using unmanned aerial vehicle-assisted rainwater collection during precipitation events. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.title: Patterns of insecticide resistance in Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus in different cities across Cameroon
papers.authors: Borel Djiappi-Tchamen, Carine Djapoum Theno, Stella Mariette Nana-Ndjangwo, Konstantinos Mavridis, Sofia Balaska
papers.abstract: The increasing frequency of arboviral diseases' outbreaks in Cameroon necessitates evidence-based vector control. However, the efficacy of chemical control interventions is seriously threatened by the rapid evolution of insecticide resistance in Aedes vector populations. This study investigated the insecticide resistance profiles of Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus across ecologically diverse cities in Cameroon. Aedes larvae were collected from April to November 2024 in eight major cities representing diverse ecological landscapes across Cameroon: Yaoundé (Congo-Guinean equatorial forest); Douala and Kribi (coastal areas); Nkongsamba, Bafoussam, Mbouda, and Maroua (highland areas); and Bertoua (sub-tropical/savanna transition zone). World Health Organization (WHO) insecticide susceptibility bioassays were conducted on F1 adults against pyrethroids (0.75% permethrin, 0.05% deltamethrin), carbamates (0.1% propoxur, 0.1% bendiocarb), and organophosphates (0.05% pirimiphos-methyl). Methods: In June 2016, a total of 30 toxic element samples were taken from surface soils to examine their contents of lead (Pb), Zinc (Zn), Copper (Cu), Nickel (Ni), Arsenic (As), Chromium (Cr), and Cadmium (Cd). The samples were collected from 0 to 20 cm depth and measured using Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy (AAS) (PG990 Model). papers.abstract: Campylobacter is a constant concern in ensuring food safety, as it is one of the most common pathogens in food. The main source of Campylobacter species in food is poultry meat, and the primary production of this meat is a critical point where measures need to be taken to reduce its presence in the food chain. Therefore, poultry slaughterhouses are recognized as places where it is necessary to implement measures to control and reduce the number of Campylobacter spp. Food business operators are obliged to ensure greater hygiene on the slaughter line, through the inspection of equipment for each step of slaughter and the application of regular cleaning protocols. Continuous monitoring of the presence and abundance of Campylobacter spp. on the slaughter line provides data on the validity of hygiene control measures in the slaughterhouse, as well as the data needed to assess the microbiological risk in poultry meat. papers.title: Major pests of fruit and berry crops in the western region of Azerbaijan and environmentally safe control methods
papers.authors: Tunzale Isgandarova
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of Green Economy and Optimization Research
papers.abstract: In recent years, clearly observable global climate change in Azerbaijan, as in various geographical regions of the world, together with the expansion of intensive fruit orchards, has become one of the major factors contributing to the spread of diverse pest organisms, reduced crop productivity, and deterioration in the quality of agricultural products. In this context, studying pests of fruit and berry crops, determining their distribution patterns, and implementing environmentally safe control methods represent important components of modern plant protection. The aim of this study was to identify the most widespread pests affecting major fruit and berry crops cultivated in the Western region of Azerbaijan, particularly in the Ganja-Dashkasan and Gazakh-Tovuz economic regions, to assess their biological characteristics, distribution patterns, and harmful effects on plants, and to substantiate environmentally safe pest management and control measures. papers.authors: Cai Yihan, Ririko Koido, Nagai Chihiro, Hirota Mitsuru, 0000001397
papers.abstract: Wild boar (Sus scrofa) is one of the most widely distributed wild ungulates, and its populations are increasing and expanding globally due to socioeconomic change, reduced predator pressure, and climate warming. Rooting, a characteristic foraging behavior in which wild boars overturn litter, vegetation, and soil, is a major disturbance in forest ecosystems and can alter soil properties, biotic communities, ecosystem processes, and ecosystem services. In this literature review, we synthesize current knowledge of wild boar rooting in forest ecosystems. We first summarize the drivers of rooting regimes. We then review rooting-induced changes in soil physical and chemical properties, the community structure of soil microbes, invertebrates, and understory vegetation, as well as ecosystem processes and functions, including carbon and nitrogen dynamics and forest regeneration. We also discuss methodological challenges in quantifying rooting and their implications for cross-study comparisons. By reviewing previous studies, we found that both rooting regimes and their ecological impacts are highly context dependent. papers.authors: Judith Littleton, Caitlin Smith, Johnny A. Uelmen
papers.abstract: Rather than ‘novel’ zoonoses, some of our most serious threats are ‘old foes’ in particular ecological and social settings. The recent outbreak of disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo is precisely an example of this – the ‘old foes’ of malnutrition and malaria reappearing in new ways. It is important to understand how infectious diseases appear and disappear over time. This is not just the phylogeny of an infection; it is understanding how pathogens flourish as a result of human niche-construction and are mitigated by human biological and cultural adaptation. In the context of anthropogenic change and the threat of zoonoses, research into long- and short-term processes of niche construction, adaptation, and multi-species ecologies, encapsulated within One Health approaches such as One Palaeopathology, offers important insights and lessons. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.authors: Farida B. Gabdrakhmanova, Ekaterina S. Churbanova, S. Е. Solovieva, Антипин Игорь Сергеевич
papers.abstract: Hypoxia is closely associated with tumor progression, metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and diagnostic challenges. The timely detection of hypoxia in live cancer cells is critical for early cancer diagnosis and for monitoring the effectiveness of anticancer therapies. Recently, there has been growing interest in non-covalent supramolecular design strategies for the development of hypoxia-sensitive sensors and prodrugs. Unlike the widely employed covalent approach, supramolecular chemistry eliminates the need for complex and time-consuming synthetic processes. Instead, the individual components of the sensor autonomously self-assemble into the desired structure. This review provides an overview of hypoxia-targeted and hypoxia-activated supramolecular probes, along with their mechanisms of action in tumor diagnosis and therapy. The supramolecular systems considered are classified according to the use of certain classes of macrocycles. The role of macrocyclic derivatives in the various proposed approaches and the response patterns of hypoxic targets will also be analyzed. papers.authors: Szandra László
papers.source: OpenAlex / SZTE Repository of Dissertations (University of Szeged)
papers.abstract: Psychomotor alterations may represent an important symptom dimension of major psychiatric disorders. Actigraphy enables the objective assessment of motor activity and rest–activity rhythms in naturalistic settings. The aim of this dissertation was to investigate psychomotor patterns associated with the schizophrenia and bipolar spectra using detailed actigraphic feature extraction and machine learning methods. The dissertation is based on two cross-sectional studies. In the first study, we examined the actigraphic profiles of individuals without a psychiatric diagnosis who were characterised by cyclothymic temperament (CFG) or positive schizotypal traits (PSF), compared with controls. In the second study, using two independent databases, we analysed the model patterns of the PSF group and individuals with chronic schizophrenia (CS), each relative to their respective control group. Models based on combinations of detailed actigraphic features distinguished the psychometric groups from controls more accurately than models based on simple activity measures. papers.title: Effect of sampling on the descriptive distributions of correlated random walks
papers.authors: Joseph D. Bailey, Jessica Claridge
papers.abstract: Abstract Random walks are commonly used to model movement throughout the sciences, from the motion of particles and molecules to the observed behaviour of animals and crowds. The correlated random walk, which assumes a level of persistence between movement directions, has become ubiquitous in the analysis and modelling of movement in recent times. Whilst many properties of the correlated random walk are known, there are still many which are not fully understood and, therefore, under-utilised in movement data analysis. Here we consider the effect that sub-sampling has on the descriptive distributions of correlated random walks. Our work demonstrates the connection between the distributions of turning angles and step-lengths that characterise a correlated random walk, along with the resulting distributions found after sub-sampling. We provide examples for where this approach could aid in movement analysis as well as determining future ways the work could be extended.

papers.title: Recent Progress on Limonoids: The Potential, Challenges, and Insights of Chemistry and Biology
papers.authors: Tianze Li, Min Lv, Hui Xu
papers.abstract: Limonoids are an important class of highly oxygenated triterpenoids containing a distinctive 4,4,8-trimethyl-17-furanylsteroid skeleton. To date, over 2700 members, including azadirachtin, toosendanin, limonin, obacunone, nomilin, harrisonin, nimbolide, gedunin, salannin, nimbin, khayanolide, xylocarpin, swietenine, rocaglamide, trichilin, vilasinin, etc., have been isolated from citrus fruits and the plants of the Rutaceae and Meliaceae families. They play a significant role in the discovery of novel drug and pesticide candidates owing to their wide range of biological activities, such as protective, anti-inflammatory, anti-cancer, antimicrobial, and insecticidal properties. Therefore, their potential, challenges, and insights into the chemistry and biology of triterpenoid-type limonoids have recently garnered much attention. The focus of this review is not only to summarize the isolation, total synthesis, and structural modifications of limonoid-type natural products as potential therapeutic and pesticidal agents, but also to highlight the underlying mechanisms of their pharmacological effects from 2017 to 2025. papers.title: Invasive rats and threatened lizards on islands: a DNA metabarcoding approach to assess dietary spectra and trophic interactions on the Aeolian archipelago
papers.authors: Leonardo Vignoli, Emanuele Berrilli, Benedetta Gambioli, Diana S. Vasconcelos, Giulia Simbula
papers.abstract: Abstract Island ecosystems often host endemics that are highly vulnerable to invasive species. In the Mediterranean biodiversity hotspot, the Endangered Aeolian wall lizard Podarcis raffonei is undergoing severe population decline. Its largest remaining population, on Vulcano Island, dropped by c. 60% from 2017 to 2022. A newly identified threat is the invasive black rat Rattus rattus , recently recorded at high densities in the area. Using DNA metabarcoding of faecal samples, we investigated potential trophic interactions between rats and lizards on Vulcano and provided a detailed characterization of the lizard’s diet across three populations. Podarcis raffonei primarily consumed arthropods (65.7%), particularly Hymenoptera, Hemiptera and Lepidoptera, but also a significant proportion of plant matter (34.3%) including Asterales, Fabales and Poales. Rats exhibited a similarly broad diet; they showed a limited dietary overlap with lizards for animal resources but a high dietary overlap for plant resources. No lizard DNA was found in rat faeces. papers.title: Optimal Control Analysis and Cost‐Effectiveness Calculations of Chickenpox Transmission Dynamics
papers.authors: Ahuod S. Alsheri, Hegagi Mohamed Ali, Essam M. Elsaid, Mohamed Rabea Eid, W. S. Hassanin
papers.source: OpenAlex / Optimal Control Applications and Methods
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study develops and analyses a mathematical model for chickenpox transmission dynamics. The model's basic properties, including positivity, boundedness, and stability of disease‐free and endemic equilibria, are rigorously established. The basic reproduction number is derived, and sensitivity analysis identifies the most sensitive parameters. An optimal control problem is formulated with four time‐dependent controls (preventive measures, vaccination, pharmaceutical interventions, and non‐pharmaceutical treatments). Numerical simulations using a forward‐backward sweep method (FBSM) are conducted. Several control scenarios that resulted from the intersection of the recommended controls to clarify the impact of these controls and explore the most effective way to halt the disease's progress are presented. Moreover, the cost‐effectiveness analysis is presented to offer a quantitative comparison between the suggested five control scenarios. papers.title: Small patches, big differences: How landscape structure shapes Scolytinae communities in pine plantations
papers.authors: Mariano P. Grilli, Eleonora Cresta, Stefano Speranza, Romina Fachinetti
papers.abstract: Abstract Landscape structure shapes herbivorous insect distribution and abundance, yet its effects on scolytine beetles in exotic pine plantations remain poorly understood. We analysed patch‐scale (patch area, Euclidean nearest‐neighbour distance) and landscape‐scale (total core area of pine, mean nearest‐neighbour distance) metrics on the abundance of nine Scolytinae species in fragmented pine plantations of central Córdoba, Argentina. We used generalised linear mixed models (GLMMs) with a negative binomial distribution and multimodel inference (AICc‐based model averaging) to assess the effects of patch‐scale (area, isolation) and landscape‐scale (total pine cover, mean inter‐patch distance) metrics on the abundance of each species. The analyses revealed contrasting responses structured by ecological guild. The pine‐specialist bark beetle Hylurgus ligniperda showed higher abundance in landscapes with greater connectivity (shorter mean inter‐patch distances), reflecting its long‐distance dispersal capacity. Methods: Six indoor/outdoor stations were established in three high-traffic districts of Tehran. Each station was sampled with six replicates in winter 2018 (36 samples in total). papers.title: Application of medical gases in prevention and treatment of electromagnetic radiation injury.
papers.authors: Yun Xing, Fengxu Chen, Gonggeng Liu, Shijun Bao, Xujian Zhang
papers.abstract: The widespread proliferation of electromagnetic technologies in communications, healthcare, and daily life poses increasing risks of radiation-induced tissue injury. Mitigating these deleterious effects remains a formidable challenge. Recently, medical gases, including molecular hydrogen (H2), hydrogen sulfide (H2S), carbon monoxide (CO), nitric oxide (NO), and hyperbaric oxygen, have emerged as a promising therapeutic modality with radioprotective potential. These gases exert their effects through integrated, anti-inflammatory, anti-apoptotic, and mitochondrial-protective mechanisms. Specifically, the endogenous gasotransmitters (CO, NO, and H2S) modulate precise signaling networks, while the exogenous interventions (H2, and hyperbaric oxygen) function primarily through direct radical scavenging or the induction of hormetic stress responses. This review evaluates the research progress of these five medical gases in preventing and treating injuries across the electromagnetic spectrum. H2 possesses the broadest evidence base, particularly in radiofrequency and ultraviolet protection. H2S and CO demonstrate potent efficacy in addressing ultraviolet-induced skin and retinal damage. papers.abstract: Hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) is an acute exanthema disease caused by a viral infection which is generally self-limiting, most often caused by Coxsackievirus A16 and Enterovirus 71, and more often attacks children under five years of age. Problem: Transmission within the family through direct contact with secretions or lesion fluid from infected individuals is a recognized transmission route, however case reports that specifically state the possibility of intrafamilial transmission in children under two years old are still rare in the literature. Case report: We report a case of HFMD in a 15 month old boy who was brought to the outpatient facility with complaints of reddish rashes around the mouth, hands and feet since two days previously, preceded by fever as a prodromal symptom. Physical examination showed maculopapular and vesicular lesions in the perioral region, right wrist, and bilateral lower extremities, with generalized distribution and miliary to lenticular size. A history of close contact with an older sibling who experienced similar symptoms approximately one week previously supports the possibility of intrafamilial transmission between siblings. papers.authors: Pingzhi Zhao, Jiangchun Hu, Jia Zhou, Ru‐Bin Chen, Jianhua Zhao
papers.abstract: Abstract The black soil region of Northeast China is a critical area for maize production in China. However, the long‐term continuous cropping, coupled with residue‐driven pathogen carryover, soil organic matter depletion, nutrient imbalance, and climate variability, has increased maize vulnerability to diseases. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the integrated regulation of soil, microbiomes, and plant immunity for maize disease management in this region. It assesses the physicochemical properties of the soil, the microbiota, and plant immune responses. Particular attention is paid to current biological control approaches. These plant immunity‐ and microbiome‐based strategies include beneficial microbe‐mediated immune priming, activation of induced systemic resistance, modulation of plant hormone signaling networks, RNA interference (RNAi)‐based immune regulation, and microbiome‐assisted enhancement of disease resistance. The underlying mechanisms include recruitment of beneficial microorganisms, suppression of pathogen growth and virulence, stabilization of protective microbial networks, activation of plant immune signaling, and enhancement of stress resilience. papers.authors: Kumar Anil, Bhupendra Koul, K Subhash
papers.abstract: Vegetables are the major food source for nutritional security for the teeming millions across the globe. Unfortunately, the growth and development of vegetable crops face yield reduction due to the infestation of notorious sedentary endoparasites, root-knot nematodes (RKN, Meloidogyne spp.). The RKN substantially harm the vegetable crops (20–100 %) culminating in huge economic losses to the growers, becoming a serious threat to the world agricultural sector. Chemical-based nematicides are effective to a certain extent but are costly, unsafe for humans and animals and subject to various regulations. Hence, it is crucial to use green and sustainable approaches for managing RKN infection. Approaches such as cultural practices, application of cover/antagonistic crops, use of organic amendments, nanoparticles (NPs) and chemical nematicides have been deployed for management of RKN. However, application of biocontrol agents is a safer, more reliable, cost-effective and promising alternative method for management of RKN. After 70 days, plants were harvested, and plant and soil Cd were measured using AAS (atomic absorption spectrometry). In addition, the degradation percentage of diesel oil in soil was determined. Results: Soil application of MWCNs at the rate of 2% (W/W) significantly increased the biodegradation of diesel oil in the soil in the drought and salinity (6 dS/m) stress by 11.3% and 15.6%, respectively. papers.title: Before Qualia, Strategic Existence Begins
papers.authors: Angelina Inesia-Forde
papers.abstract: Before evolution can select anything, a physically possible causal architecture must already exist for selection to exploit. The T4 bacteriophage, a mindless nanoscale machine whose structure executes functions that map onto both empowering and disempowering strategies in Forde's framework of social dynamics, demonstrates this principle at the nanoscale. The strategies mapped include security, knowledge, hope, fairness, unity, and dignity, alongside their darker counterparts: nativism, hierarchy, misinformation, subjugation, dehumanization, and fear. Each concept is paired with a specific biological mechanism, virion stability, irreversible adsorption, superinfection exclusion, among others, showing that the mapping is grounded in observable structure. These mappings do not reify nonhuman organisms or attribute human qualities to mindless machines. They are structural descriptions: the concepts name functions that the architecture performs, not feelings that the organism experiences. This reframes a persistent gap in philosophy of mind: qualia have long been debated while the physical architecture that must bound it has been neglected. papers.authors: Dhruv Sahni, Imran Ahmad, David Brian Kingsmore, E. Murio, Andrew Jackson
papers.abstract: Background: Adults with a modified lower urinary tract (MLUT) represent a growing but understudied population in renal transplantation. Concerns regarding long-term graft survival, infection, and urological morbidity persist, yet adult-specific outcome synthesis and clinically useful guidance are lacking. Methods: We performed a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-compliant systematic review of studies reporting posttransplant outcomes in adults with abnormal or surgically MLUT anatomy. Primary outcomes were 1- and 5-y graft and patient survival. Secondary outcomes included urological complications. Given substantial heterogeneity, data were synthesized narratively. Results: Twenty-four studies, including 511 MLUT recipients, were identified. Most were retrospective single-center series, and only a minority included comparator cohorts. Several studies included mixed adult-pediatric cohorts where adult-only outcomes could not be separated. papers.title: The Pass-Through of Retail Crime
papers.authors: Carl Hase, Johannes Kasinger
papers.source: OpenAlex / American Economic Journal Economic Policy
papers.abstract: This paper shows retailers increase prices in response to organized retail crime. We match store-level crime data to scanner data from the universe of transactions for cannabis retailers in Washington state. Using quasi-experimental variation from robberies and burglaries, we find a 1.7–1.8 percent price increase at victimized stores and nearby competitors. This rise is not driven by short-to-medium-term demand changes but is consistent with crime-related cost shocks. Effects are larger for independent stores and less concentrated markets. We estimate crime imposes a 1 percent “hidden” unit tax on affected stores, implying $30.7 million in additional social costs, primarily borne by consumers. (JEL D22, H22, H76, K42, L81)

papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a global threat to humankind, affecting food safety, health, and the economy. Moreover, it is evolving rapidly, resulting from the misuse and overuse of antibiotics in healthcare and agriculture a result which has emerged as a One Health challenge. It alters food systems by creating threats to food safety, food security, and public health. Such resistant microorganisms have the ability to persist and spread in the food systems, animals, water, and the environment. Such microorganisms are further sustained by the production of biofilms. There is increased demand for safe and sustainable alternatives as a result of the limited applicability of conventional antibiotics and chemical preservatives. This review evaluates their applicability in different aspects of food safety and preservation and in mitigating AMR.
